headline: High-risk shared git workspace and unverified MCP/REST pathways create prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-error exposure between Aider and OpenBBTerminal.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes git-tracked files and shares state via a git repo, so OpenBBTerminal content placed in that workspace can be re-ingested as instructions. OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP/REST/stdio surfaces, but its exact provenance controls are undocumented here, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal writes attacker-controlled text into the shared repo or a file Aider later reads
IF Aider is run on content from OpenBBTerminal without a provenance filter
mitigations: Separate the repos or mount read-only copies for one agent
Disable automatic file re-ingestion for shared artifacts
Add a provenance banner to files exchanged between agents
Review any MCP/REST payloads before copying them into the repo

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider can read the filesystem and handles source code and git history; OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data and can expose it through APIs/MCP. A shared workspace or copied files could leak sensitive financial or licensed data from B into Aider outputs, though the exact default sharing is not fully documented.
conditions: IF financial or licensed data from OpenBBTerminal is placed in files Aider can read
IF Aider is connected to the same workspace or git repo as OpenBBTerminal
mitigations: Keep financial datasets outside Aider's workspace
Use separate OS users or containers
Redact sensitive fields before handoff
Restrict Aider to a narrow subdirectory
Audit git diffs for accidental data inclusion

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider has unrestricted filesystem write and modify_git_state, while OpenBBTerminal can use MCP and REST APIs and is described as connect-once-consume-everywhere. In a shared repo or shared mutable resource, concurrent writes and state changes can collide without locking, making destructive conflicts plausible by default.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository or mutable workspace
IF OpenBBTerminal MCP/API actions and Aider git edits occur concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working tree
Serialize writes with a lock file
Require manual merge review before commits
Disable concurrent sessions on the same repo
Use branch-per-agent workflows

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider can generate and commit code changes, and OpenBBTerminal can consume data through APIs/MCP. If OpenBBTerminal treats Aider-produced files or summaries as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream financial analysis or actions. The pairwise interaction is undocumented, so uncertainty favors medium over low.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal ingests Aider-authored files or summaries without verification
IF Aider commits incorrect code or notes that OpenBBTerminal later uses as input
mitigations: Require source citations in handoffs
Add a human verification step before OpenBBTerminal consumes Aider output
Mark Aider outputs as draft-only
Keep analysis and code-editing tasks separate
Log and diff all handoff artifacts

E_compliance.rationale: Aider handles source code and git history, while OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data. If regulated financial or licensed content is moved into Aider's repo, retention and redistribution rules may diverge. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so this is a policy-mismatch risk rather than high severity.
conditions: IF licensed or regulated financial data is copied into Aider-managed git history
IF retention or deletion requirements differ between the two workflows
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of git history
Add a retention policy for shared artifacts
Use separate storage for licensed datasets
Document deletion/export procedures
Review compliance requirements before handoff
